purpose: The trusted registry of terms documents B1 may capture, keyed by (sourceId, candidateDocId). Every capture resolves against this file before acquisition or publication. Metadata only -- no document bytes are stored here.
rules: A caller may name a (sourceId, candidateDocId). A caller may NEVER supply the document URL, the declared media type, the allowed final URLs or the identity expectations: those are owned here, or the identity guard checks the caller's expectation against the caller's own document and proves nothing.

No record may declare which document is operative or governing. That is a legal conclusion, it belongs to a human, and the schema refuses the field rather than leaving it unset -- so promoting one would require a visible manifest diff.
observationState=NOT_OBSERVED means nobody has opened it. Such a record carries no identityExpectations at all. Registering a document that exists is honest; describing its contents unseen is not.
A source with no known terms document records an empty candidate list AND a reason, so a later reader can tell 'none found' from 'nobody looked'.

sources.noCandidatesReason: www.technogym.com returns HTTP 403 to programmatic requests, so no terms document could be located. Not 'no terms exist' -- 'none identified'. A human retrieving the footer link in a browser would close this.

requiredMarkers: Use of the Site and Standards of Conduct
identityExpectations.markerNote: Section headings and clause vocabulary actually seen in the document on the date above. Factual: they assert what the DOCUMENT is, never whether its terms permit anything.

candidates.note: A second Life Fitness legal document, reached from the site's own footer. NOT opened. Whether it is distinct from terms_of_use, and which of the two governs, are both open questions B1 does not answer.
